claims.statement: California’s earthquake overlay has separate regulatory and contract layers: CDI bulletins govern the insurer’s offer, notice, response, filing, records, and claims practices, while earthquake coverage still depends on the policy and an attached earthquake endorsement; internal underwriting guidance does not itself grant coverage.

The source set identifies HO 01 04 California Amendatory Endorsement 2021-06 as effective 2021-06-01 for California property and interests, with precedence over conflicting policy language to the extent permitted by California law.

CDI-2014-06 is effective 2014-06-30 and is superseded by CDI-2022-03 for policies effective on or after 2022-03-14, while remaining in force for policies written under the earlier bulletin. CDI-2022-03 is effective from 2022-03-14 and requires offers and procedures to follow the applicable effective-date position.

Under CDI-2014-06, an admitted insurer offering or issuing California residential property insurance must make a clear, timely, verifiable, separate earthquake offer, disclose that the underlying policy may not cover earthquake damage, explain material coverages and limitations, and remain responsible when another lawful insurer presents the coverage.

CDI-2014-06 requires the offer notice when residential property insurance is offered and again with a renewal offer; the notice must be clear, conspicuous, understandable, distinguish the offer from existing coverage, explain acceptance and declination, disclose material limitations and the deductible, and preserve readable electronic delivery when used.

For the CDI-2014-06 position, the offered earthquake coverage must disclose a 10% seismic deductible and explain its application; acceptance must have a reasonable communication method, silence cannot establish acceptance without affirmative authorization, and offer and response records must be preserved.

CDI-2014-06 applies its claims standards to claims received on or after its effective date and requires prompt acknowledgment, reasonable investigation, qualified handling, written claim decisions stating the policy basis, distinction between covered and noncovered damage, undisputed-payment handling, and documented claim files; it states no numeric acknowledgment or payment deadline.

CDI-2014-06 requires filing of the earthquake offer and related materials before use, identification of applicable policy forms, presentation method, and effective dates, consistency between filed and delivered materials, and discontinuation of noncompliant materials.

Under CDI-2022-03, an insurer must make a written earthquake offer when issuing or renewing eligible residential property insurance; the offer may be electronic only with consent and must identify the insurer, related policy, property, limits, material terms, exclusions, conditions, premium or rating basis, and disclosed underwriting conditions.

CDI-2022-03 requires the offer to state a 15% seismic deductible of applicable covered loss and explain its operation; acceptance must be affirmative, silence is insufficient, acceptance and declination require written confirmation, and the insurer must preserve delivery, response, and ineligibility records.

CDI-2022-03 requires a meaningful opportunity to consider the offer, prohibits withholding it until after the related transaction, and requires a written nonrenewal notice at least 75 days before nonrenewal takes effect; the earthquake offer must remain distinct from cancellation or nonrenewal communications when combining them would mislead.

CDI-2022-03 requires prompt earthquake-claim acknowledgment, reasonable investigation, qualified and clear handling, relevant information requests, written explanations for denials or limitations, payment without unreasonable delay after the amount is determined, undisputed payment while other portions remain under review, supplemental-information opportunity, supervision, and claim records; it states no numeric claim deadline.

CDI-2022-03 requires filing of all offer-related forms and materials, including applications, elections, rejections, and acknowledgments, and prohibits use of unfiled or superseded materials; effective filings must be applied consistently and the insurer remains responsible for delegated offer functions.

HO 01 04 2021-06 states a California earthquake deductible of 15% of applicable covered property value, applies it to covered earthquake loss, groups damage from the same earthquake occurrence, and requires 100% insured-to-value for replacement-cost settlement of a covered building.

HO 01 04 supplies contractual timing controls distinct from CDI offer rules: deductible-change notice must precede application without a stated numeric advance period; cancellation requires at least 10 days for nonpayment or 20 days for another reason; nonrenewal requires at least 75 days before expiration; and claims have 15-day acknowledgment, 40-business-day decision-or-explanation, and 30-business-day payment periods.

The multistate HO 04 54 2009-04 endorsement is effective 2009-04-01 and remains relevant to policies written under it; it treats related earth shocks from the same movement as one earthquake loss, states a 5% earthquake deductible applied to covered loss after the covered loss is determined, and requires prompt notice within 90 days after discovery. Its supplied wording does not state a dwelling-limit or one-deductible-per-occurrence basis.

The multistate HO 04 54 2021-12 earthquake endorsement is effective 2021-12-01, states an applicable earthquake deductible percentage of 10% applied to covered Earthquake loss before payment and not to uncovered property or loss, and requires prompt notice plus a report within 90 days after the loss occurs. Its supplied wording does not state a Coverage A basis or a single aggregate across every property class.

The explicit form-to-bulletin implementation link is HO 01 04 T.57, which directs that its provision be applied as required by CDI-2022-03 B.2; because T.57 is in the windstorm-and-hail section, it does not itself create earthquake coverage or prove that the offer, affirmative authorization, or filing was completed.

Internal underwriting guidance requires review of earthquake attachment location and construction characteristics and the quake deductible, prohibits unauthorized alteration, waiver, or negotiation of the quake deductible, and requires a complete record of facts, sources, analysis, and authority action for California referrals and adverse decisions.

The supplied HO-3 Homeowners 3—Special Form 2024-03 is effective 2024-03-01 and excludes earth movement, including earthquake, in its property and liability exclusions; earthquake coverage therefore requires the applicable attached endorsement and California contract overlay. Its base conditions separately provide a 90-day proof-of-loss period after request and payment within 60 days after agreement, final judgment, or appraisal.

The HO 04 54 2009-04 endorsement is superseded by HO 04 54 2021-12 for policies effective on or after 2021-12-01, but remains relevant to policies written under the earlier edition; the attached edition must control the earthquake grant, deductible, exclusions, and claim conditions.

The supplied HO 04 54 2021-12 wording contains a grant/exclusion tension: W.1 describes direct physical loss including specified earthquake-caused ground movement and resulting damage, while W.4 contains broad earth-movement exclusions referring to earthquake loss, shaking, tremors, aftershocks, and shifting; the complete issued form and applicable California amendment must be analyzed rather than treating all earth movement as categorically covered or excluded.

California internal underwriting controls, separate from contract coverage and CDI requirements, limit delegated line-underwriter binding authority to $1,000,000, prohibit issuing Coverage A above $2,000,000, and require valuation support for 100% insured-to-value before offering replacement-cost settlement; these thresholds are underwriting controls and must not be confused with the HO-3 80% contract threshold or HO 01 04’s 100% condition.

The California overlay must reconcile, rather than blend, the different 15% deductible bases stated by the sources: CDI-2022-03 describes the offer as 15% of applicable covered loss, while HO 01 04 states a contractual 15% of applicable covered property value; the filed offer and complete issued policy package govern the operational application.
